questions.stem: A dispatcher hints yesterday's roster to today's model, but two crews are on leave today and that roster breaks today's limits. What does CP-SAT do with the hint?

options.text: It refuses the model as invalid, as a hint that breaks a rule is an error
options.says: A hint may be infeasible; the GridCap run with a hint that overspent the cut budgets still solved, with status FEASIBLE.

options.text: It returns yesterday's roster, as hinted values are kept as given
options.says: Hints are fixed only with fix_variables_to_their_hinted_value; by default a hint is a suggestion.

options.text: It treats the roster as a suggestion and searches for rosters within the rules
options.says: Right: a hint is never a constraint; the GridCap run with an infeasible hint found plans that kept the cut budgets.

options.text: It reports INFEASIBLE, as the search starts from the hinted roster
options.says: The hinted run on the cut budgets reported FEASIBLE plans; an infeasible hint does not make the model infeasible.

origin.section: A Hint Is a Suggested Plan, Never a Constraint

questions.stem: To test last year's 12-project plan, you hint those 12 start variables at 1, give the other 30 no hint, set fix_variables_to_their_hinted_value, and get OPTIMAL. What has the solve shown?

options.text: That the 12 fit together in a plan that keeps this year's rules
options.says: Right: only hinted variables are fixed, so the other 30 stay free and the solver may switch some on.

options.text: That last year's plan, as it stood, keeps this year's rules
options.says: The 30 unhinted variables were free, so the plan the solver checked may differ from last year's.

options.text: That last year's 12 projects make this year's best plan
options.says: With variables fixed, OPTIMAL only means best among the plans left, not among all plans.

options.text: That nothing is known yet, as the setting rejects a partial hint
options.says: The setting fixes the hinted variables and leaves the rest free; the CP-SAT docs allow partial hints.

origin.section: Fixing Every Variable to Its Hint Tests Whether the Hint Is Feasible

questions.stem: A maintenance model with 40 flagged rules, solved with one worker, is INFEASIBLE, and sufficient_assumptions_for_infeasibility returns all 40 indices. What does that tell you?

options.text: The 40 rules together clash, and each one of them is needed for it
options.says: On GridCap all 28 flags came back, yet the deletion filter left 3 of them.

options.text: The 40 rules together clash, and whether fewer would is not yet known
options.says: Right: the set is sufficient, not minimal; GridCap's 28 named flags shrank to a minimal clash of 3.

options.text: The call misread the solve, as happens on models with many rules
options.says: The GridCap call named all 28 flags and was correct: those 28 rules together are infeasible.

options.text: The model holds no real clash, as a real one names a few rules
options.says: The model is infeasible; naming every rule is a true but unhelpful answer, as GridCap's 28 of 28 shows.

origin.section: sufficient_assumptions_for_infeasibility Names Flags That Clash, Not Always the Fewest
